newsitem.title: USA: Southern Carolina to buy United Carolina for $985 million.
newsitem.headline: Southern Carolina to buy United Carolina for $985 million.

text.p: Southern National Corp. said Monday it plans to acquire United Carolina Bancshares Corp. for $985 million in a deal that would lead to 1,000 job cuts through attrition or early retirement.

The bank would take a charge against earnings of up to $50 million to pay for expenses including retirement packages, said Southern National Chairman John Allison. The combined company would have 9,500 workers.
The stock transaction between the two North Carolina-based banks was valued at $40.01 a share, a price Wall Street analysts characterised as rich but fair.
Shares of UCB soared $8.50 to $36 in Nasdaq trading while Southern National finished down $1.75 at $33.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Under the agreement, Whiteville, N.C.-based UCB's investors would get 1.135 shares of Winston-Salem, N.C.-based Southern National stock for each of their UCB common shares.

If approved by shareholders and federal regulators, assets for the combined Southern National would exceed $25 billion, compared with $21.1 billion at the end of the third quarter. Savings could top $65 million annually, Allison said.

The merger is expected to be completed in the second quarter of 1997, and result in a one-time charge of between $40 million and $50 million to cover merger-related expenses for the severance programme, as well as closing branches in the estimated 80 areas where the two banking operations overlap.
Southern National operates 425 banking offices in 219 cities throughout the Carolinas and Virginia, while UCB operates 153 offices in 89 communities in the Carolinas.
Customers of mid-size banks such as UCB are not offered the vast automated teller machine network or mutual funds put forth by NationsBank Corp. and First Union Corp.
Allison, who took the helm of Southern National after the 1994 acquisition of mid-sized Branch Banking & Trust Financial Corp., described the UCB deal as walking the "razor's edge."

He said the more recent round of acquisitions made by the bank -- a finance company and insurance firm -- asserts the bank's goal to remain independent and increases its attraction to any possible suitors.
Once the merger is complete, the bank expects its efficiency ratio, or what it costs to earn $1, will be about 50 percent, down from 53.3 percent in the third quarter.
